 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Rajeev Ranjan Prasad
Oral Order
2 21-07-2023 Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned APP for the State.

2. The petitioner, in the present case, is seeking pre-arrest bail in connection with Mahishi P.S. Case No. 372 of 2022 registered for the offences punishable under Sections 420 of the Indian Penal Code,
Section 7 of Essential Commodities Act, 1955 and Section 3(i)(c) of the Fertilizer Control Order,
1985.
He has no criminal antecedent as stated in paragraph '3' of the application.

3. As per the prosecution story, the informant, who is the Fertilizer Inspector-cum-Agriculture Coordinator, Mahishi Block, has alleged that on information that fertilizer are being illegally transported from Tractor for Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.33075 of 2023(2) dt.21-07-2023 black marketing, when he reached at the alleged place he saw that villagers were crowded and surrounded a loaded tractor along with driver.
The driver was apprehended and he disclosed his name as Rampreet Yadav and also disclosed that one Kishore Yadav and other farmers called him for taking their fertilizers.
The informant further alleged that from the seized tractor the fertilizer of different company and other items were recovered.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the allegation against the petitioner is false and flimsy.
He has been made accused on the mere statement of the apprehended tractor driver.

sentences.text: It is submitted that the petitioner is running a licensee shop and in fact he had sold the seized fertilizers and other items to some of the farmers.

6. Learned A.P.P. for the State submits that there is a very serious allegation against the petitioner that he being a licensee shop owner for making available the fertilizers and other agriculture related items to the farmers had indulged in black marketing of the fertilizers and medicines.

7. It is submitted that the villagers of Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.33075 of 2023(2)
dt.21-07-2023 Pokharbhinda where the shop of the petitioner is situated had surrounded the tractor on which the fertilizers were laden and they were agitated on the black marketing of the fertilizers.
8.

It is further submitted that the shop is situated in village Pokharbhinda, Ward No. 13, but at this stage, the petitioner is looking to justify his black marketing by showing some receipts which are in the name of some persons of another village and ward.
9.
It is submitted that over the period black marketing of fertilizers and agriculture related items has become a big menace and it is one of the modes of corruption.
The ultimate sufferers are the farmers who are compelled to purchase the fertilizers in black market.

10. Having heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned APP for the State, upon noticing the kind of materials present in the F.I.R. itself, the admission of the tractor driver as well as the petitioner that the seized fertilizers in huge quantity were being taken from the shop of the petitioner, the allegation being that of indulging in black marketing, in these materials, this Court is not inclined to Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.33075 of 2023(2) dt.21-07-2023 grant privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.
11. Prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner is, thus, refused.

12. In case, the petitioner surrenders and prays for regular bail in the learned court below within a period of four weeks from today, his prayer for regular bail shall be considered on it's own merit without being prejudiced by the order of this Court.

(Rajeev Ranjan Prasad, J) Rajeev/-
